// features/milestone-burndown.md: chart, summary, changes, PR toggle, collapse, done/closed/empty/no-due states
import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '../fixtures.ts';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {capture, note} from '../evidence.ts';
import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateIssue, apiCreateMilestone, apiCreateRepo, apiHeaders, baseUrl, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

type Point = {date: string, remaining: number, scope: number};

const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
const dueOn = () => new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 864e5);
const counts = (points: Point[]) => points.map(({remaining, scope}) => ({remaining, scope}));

async function apiSend(page: Page, method: string, path: string, data: unknown) {
  const response = await page.request.fetch(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1${path}`, {method, headers: apiHeaders(), data});
  expect(response.ok()).toBe(true);
  return response.json();
}

async function seedRepo(page: Page) {
  const repo = `e2e-burndown-${randomString(8)}`;
  await Promise.all([apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repo}), login(page)]);
  return repo;
}

// opens the milestone page and returns the burndown JSON its chart fetched
async function openMilestone(page: Page, repo: string, id: number, query = '') {
  const [response] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes(`/milestone/${id}/burndown${query}`)),
    page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/milestone/${id}`),
  ]);
  return response.json();
}

const chart = (page: Page) => page.locator('#milestone-burndown-chart');
const summary = (page: Page) => chart(page).locator('.milestone-burndown-summary');

test('a new milestone charts its first day and toggles pull requests', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner, repo, title: 'M1', dueOn: dueOn()});
  for (const title of ['A', 'B', 'C']) await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo, title, milestone: id});
  await apiSend(page, 'PATCH', `/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/1`, {state: 'closed'});
  await apiCreateFile(page.request, owner, repo, 'x.txt', 'x', {branch: 'main', newBranch: 'feat'});
  await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/repos/${owner}/${repo}/pulls`, {head: 'feat', base: 'main', title: 'P', milestone: id});

  const issuesOnly = await openMilestone(page, repo, id);
  note('burndown', issuesOnly);
  expect(issuesOnly.status).toBe('insufficient_data');
  expect(counts(issuesOnly.points)).toEqual([{remaining: 2, scope: 3}]);
  await expect(chart(page).locator('canvas')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(summary(page)).toHaveText('A projected finish date appears after two days of history');
  await expect(chart(page).locator('canvas')).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', (await summary(page).textContent())!.trim());
  await expect(chart(page).locator('.milestone-burndown-changes')).toContainText(`Changes on ${issuesOnly.points[0].date}`);
  await expect(chart(page).locator('.milestone-burndown-changes')).toContainText('Closed: #1 A');
  await capture(page, 'before-toggle');

  const toggle = chart(page).getByRole('checkbox', {name: 'Include pull requests'});
  await expect(toggle).not.toBeChecked();
  const [response] = await Promise.all([page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes('burndown?include_pulls=1')), toggle.check()]);
  const withPulls = await response.json();
  note('burndown-pulls', withPulls);
  expect(counts(withPulls.points)).toEqual([{remaining: 3, scope: 4}]);
  expect(page.url()).toContain('include_pulls=1');
  await page.reload();
  await expect(chart(page).getByRole('checkbox', {name: 'Include pull requests'})).toBeChecked();
  await capture(page, 'after-toggle');
  await chart(page).locator('summary').first().click();
  await expect(chart(page).locator('canvas')).toBeHidden();
});

test('a milestone with everything closed shows its completion date', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner, repo, title: 'Done', dueOn: dueOn()});
  for (const title of ['D1', 'D2']) {
    const {index} = await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo, title, milestone: id});
    await apiSend(page, 'PATCH', `/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${index}`, {state: 'closed'});
  }
  const burndown = await openMilestone(page, repo, id);
  await expect(summary(page)).toHaveText(`Completed on ${burndown.points[0].date}`);
  await capture(page, 'done');
});

test('a milestone closed with open items says so', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  const due = dueOn();
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner, repo, title: 'Closed', dueOn: due});
  await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo, title: 'Still open', milestone: id});
  await apiSend(page, 'PATCH', `/repos/${owner}/${repo}/milestones/${id}`, {state: 'closed', due_on: due.toISOString()}); // without due_on the PATCH clears it
  await openMilestone(page, repo, id);
  await expect(summary(page)).toHaveText('Milestone closed with open items');
});

test('a milestone without a due date asks for one', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner, repo, title: 'NoDue'});
  await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo, title: 'ND', milestone: id});
  await openMilestone(page, repo, id);
  await expect(summary(page)).toHaveText('A projected finish date appears after two days of history · Set a due date to see the ideal line');
  await expect(chart(page).locator('canvas')).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', 'A projected finish date appears after two days of history');
});

test('an empty milestone shows a message instead of a chart', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner, repo, title: 'Empty'});
  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/milestone/${id}`);
  await expect(chart(page)).toContainText('This milestone has no issues or pull requests yet.');
  await expect(chart(page).locator('canvas')).toHaveCount(0);
  await capture(page, 'empty');
});

// features/pull-request-create.md: every entry point, toggle path, create, Files Changed, duplicate guard
import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '../fixtures.ts';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {capture} from '../evidence.ts';
import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateRepo, apiHeaders, baseUrl, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
const path = (page: Page) => page.url().replace(/^https?:\/\/[^/]+/, '');

// a repo whose feat branch the admin has just pushed, so the recent-push banner shows
async function seed(page: Page) {
  const repo = `e2e-pr-create-${randomString(8)}`;
  await Promise.all([apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repo}), login(page)]);
  await apiCreateFile(page.request, owner, repo, 'feat.txt', 'feature\n', {branch: 'main', newBranch: 'feat'});
  return {repo, web: `/${owner}/${repo}`};
}

test('the recent-push banner opens the compare page expanded', async ({page}) => {
  const {web} = await seed(page);
  await page.goto(web);
  const banner = page.locator('.ui.positive.message').filter({hasText: 'You pushed on branch'});
  await expect(banner).toBeVisible();
  await expect(banner.getByRole('link', {name: 'feat'})).toHaveAttribute('href', `${web}/src/branch/feat`);
  const button = banner.getByRole('button', {name: 'New Pull Request'});
  await expect(button).toHaveAttribute('href', `${web}/compare/main...feat?expand=1`);
  await capture(page, 'home-banner');
  await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('load'), button.click()]);
  expect(path(page)).toBe(`${web}/compare/main...feat?expand=1`);
  await expect(page.getByPlaceholder('Title')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Create Pull Request'})).toBeVisible();
  await capture(page, 'compare-expanded');
});

test('New Pull Request on the list stays collapsed until a head branch is picked', async ({page}) => {
  const {repo, web} = await seed(page);
  await page.goto(`${web}/pulls`);
  await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('load'), page.locator('.new-pr-button').click()]);
  expect(path(page)).toBe(`${web}/compare/main...main`);
  await expect(page.getByPlaceholder('Title')).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.locator('.pullrequest-form-toggle .show-panel')).toHaveCount(0);
  const head = page.locator('.choose.branch .ui.dropdown').filter({hasText: 'pull from'});
  await head.click();
  await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('load'), head.locator('.head-branch-list .item', {hasText: `${owner}/${repo}:feat`}).click()]);
  expect(path(page)).toBe(`${web}/compare/main...feat`);
  await expect(page.locator('.pullrequest-form-toggle .show-panel')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByPlaceholder('Title')).toBeHidden();
  await capture(page, 'compare-head-picked');
});

test('branch pages link to the expanded compare page', async ({page}) => {
  const {web} = await seed(page);
  await page.goto(`${web}/pulls/new/feat`);
  expect(path(page)).toBe(`${web}/compare/main...feat?expand=1`);
  await expect(page.getByPlaceholder('Title')).toBeVisible();
  await page.goto(`${web}/branches`);
  await expect(page.locator(`a[href="${web}/compare/main...feat?expand=1"]`).first()).toBeAttached();
  await page.goto(`${web}/src/branch/feat`);
  await expect(page.locator('#new-pull-request')).toHaveAttribute('href', `${web}/compare/main...feat?expand=1`);
});

test('creating a pull request opens it, and a second one for the branch is refused', async ({page}) => {
  const {repo, web} = await seed(page);
  await page.goto(`${web}/compare/main...feat`);
  await expect(page.getByText('feat.txt').first()).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByPlaceholder('Title')).toBeHidden();
  await capture(page, 'compare');
  await page.locator('.pullrequest-form-toggle .show-panel').click();
  await page.getByPlaceholder('Title').fill('Verify PR');
  await page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Create Pull Request'}).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/\/pulls\/\d+$/, {waitUntil: 'commit'});
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', {name: 'Verify PR'})).toBeVisible();
  await capture(page, 'pr');
  const pr = await (await page.request.get(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/pulls/1`, {headers: apiHeaders()})).json();
  expect({title: pr.title, head: pr.head.ref, base: pr.base.ref, state: pr.state}).toEqual({title: 'Verify PR', head: 'feat', base: 'main', state: 'open'});

  await page.goto(`${web}/pulls/1/files`);
  await expect(page.getByText('feat.txt').first()).toBeVisible();
  await capture(page, 'files');

  await page.goto(`${web}/compare/main...feat?expand=1`);
  await expect(page.getByPlaceholder('Title')).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.getByRole('link', {name: 'View Pull Request'})).toHaveAttribute('href', `${web}/pulls/1`);
  await capture(page, 'duplicate-guard');
  await page.goto(web);
  await expect(page.locator('.ui.positive.message').filter({hasText: 'You pushed on branch'})).toHaveCount(0); // the PR exists now
});

// features/shortcuts.md: S, T, Escape, input guard, ? help dialog (rows, guard, focus, close), file view T, every g sequence, timeout, dead keys, overflow g w, anonymous g n and ?
import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '../fixtures.ts';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {capture, note} from '../evidence.ts';
import {apiCreateBranch, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;

async function seedRepo(page: Page) {
  const repo = `e2e-shortcuts-${randomString(8)}`;
  await Promise.all([apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repo}), login(page)]);
  return `/${owner}/${repo}`;
}

async function press(page: Page, keys: string) {
  for (const key of keys.split(' ')) await page.keyboard.press(key);
}

// presses a shortcut that leaves the page, and waits until the next page can take one
async function goWith(page: Page, keys: string, url: RegExp) {
  await press(page, keys);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(url);
  await page.waitForLoadState('load');
}

const toBody = (page: Page) => page.waitForFunction(() => document.activeElement === document.body);
const at = (page: Page, path: string) => expect(new URL(page.url()).pathname).toBe(path);
const searchBox = (page: Page) => page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]');
const fileBox = (page: Page) => page.locator('.repo-file-search-container input');

test('s and t focus their boxes, keys typed there stay text, and Escape leaves', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  await page.goto(repo);
  await page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd[aria-keyshortcuts="t"]').waitFor({state: 'attached'});
  await page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd[aria-keyshortcuts="s"]').waitFor({state: 'attached'});
  await capture(page, 'hints');
  await press(page, 's');
  await expect(searchBox(page)).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.type('g i'); // typed into the box, not run
  await expect(searchBox(page)).toHaveValue('g i');
  at(page, repo);
  await press(page, 'Escape');
  await toBody(page);
  await expect(searchBox(page)).toHaveValue('');
  await press(page, 't');
  await expect(fileBox(page)).toBeFocused();
  await capture(page, 't-focused');
  await press(page, 'Escape');
  await toBody(page);
  await press(page, 'g s'); // a key that doesn't continue the sequence runs as a fresh press
  await expect(searchBox(page)).toBeFocused();
  await press(page, 'Escape');
  await toBody(page);
});

test('? opens the help dialog, which blocks page shortcuts and returns focus on close', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  await page.goto(repo);
  await page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd[aria-keyshortcuts="s"]').waitFor({state: 'attached'});
  const help = page.getByRole('dialog', {name: 'Keyboard shortcuts'});
  const rows = help.locator('.shortcut-help-row');
  const opener = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top form button');
  await opener.focus();
  await press(page, '?');
  await expect(help).toBeVisible();
  await expect(help.locator('h3')).toHaveText(['General', 'Repository']);
  await expect(help.locator('section').first().locator('dt')).toHaveText(['Notifications', 'Show keyboard shortcuts']);
  await expect(help.locator('section').nth(1).locator('dt')).toHaveText(['Code', 'Issues', 'Pull Requests', 'Actions', 'Wiki', 'Search code…', 'Go to file']);
  await expect(rows.filter({has: page.locator('dt', {hasText: /^Code$/})}).locator('kbd')).toHaveText(['G', 'C']);
  await capture(page, 'help-open');
  const count = await rows.count();
  await press(page, 's'); // the page behind takes no shortcut (inert alone would also stop this one)
  await expect(searchBox(page)).not.toBeFocused();
  await press(page, 'g i'); // a navigation shortcut is only stopped by the registry's dialog[open] guard
  await page.waitForTimeout(500);
  at(page, repo);
  await press(page, '?'); // a second ? leaves the dialog as it is
  await expect(help).toBeVisible();
  await expect(rows).toHaveCount(count);
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) await press(page, 'Tab');
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => Boolean(document.activeElement!.closest('dialog')))).toBe(true);
  await press(page, 'Escape');
  await expect(help).toBeHidden();
  await expect(opener).toBeFocused();
  await press(page, '?');
  await help.getByRole('button', {name: 'Close'}).click();
  await expect(help).toBeHidden();
  await expect(opener).toBeFocused();
  await searchBox(page).focus();
  await page.keyboard.type('a?'); // typed into the box, no dialog
  await expect(searchBox(page)).toHaveValue('a?');
  await expect(help).toBeHidden();
  await press(page, 'Escape');
  await toBody(page);
});

test('the file view offers t but has no s box', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  await page.goto(`${repo}/src/branch/main/README.md`);
  await page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd[aria-keyshortcuts="t"]').waitFor({state: 'attached'});
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top')).toHaveCount(0);
  await press(page, 't');
  await expect(fileBox(page)).toBeFocused();
  await capture(page, 'file-view-t-focused');
  await press(page, 'Escape');
  await toBody(page);
});

test('every g sequence opens its tab, and g c goes to the default branch', async ({page}) => {
  const repo = await seedRepo(page);
  const [, , name] = repo.split('/');
  await apiCreateBranch(page.request, owner, name, 'feature');
  await page.goto(`${repo}/src/branch/feature`);
  note('declared', await page.locator('[data-shortcut-keys]').evaluateAll((els) => els.map((e) => [(e as HTMLElement).dataset.shortcutKeys, e.getAttribute('href'), (e as HTMLElement).dataset.shortcutHref ?? null])));
  await goWith(page, 'g c', new RegExp(`${repo}$`)); // the default branch, not the browsed one

// features/notifications.md: repo and type filters, empty state, mark-all naming, bulk actions, select-all-in-view,
// navbar bell and g n entry points, filtered Read tab, bulk Mark as unread / Pin / confirmed Delete
import {test, expect} from '../fixtures.ts';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {capture, note} from '../evidence.ts';
import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateIssue, apiCreatePR, apiCreateRepo, apiCreateUser, apiUserHeaders, baseUrl, loginUser, randomString} from './utils.ts';

type Notification = {subject: {title: string}, pinned: boolean, unread: boolean};

// a fresh user with repos r1 (two issues) and r2 (an issue and a PR) that the admin filed, so four unread notifications
async function seed(page: Page) {
  const owner = `e2e-notif-${randomString(8)}`;
  await apiCreateUser(page.request, owner);
  const headers = apiUserHeaders(owner);
  await Promise.all(['r1', 'r2'].map((name) => apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name, headers}))); // created as the owner, who then watches them
  const repoIds = Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all(['r1', 'r2'].map(async (name) =>
    [name, (await (await page.request.get(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${name}`, {headers})).json()).id])));
  for (const title of ['one', 'two']) await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo: 'r1', title: `r1 ${title}`});
  await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo: 'r2', title: 'r2 one'});
  await apiCreateFile(page.request, owner, 'r2', 'x.txt', 'x', {branch: 'main', newBranch: 'feat'});
  await apiCreatePR(page.request, owner, 'r2', 'feat', 'main', 'r2 pr');
  await loginUser(page, owner);
  await expect(async () => { // a background queue writes notifications
    await page.goto('/notifications');
    await expect(rows(page)).toHaveCount(4, {timeout: 500});
  }).toPass();
  return {owner, headers, repoIds};
}

const rows = (page: Page) => page.locator('#notification_table .notifications-item');
const row = (page: Page, title: string) => rows(page).filter({hasText: title});
const bulk = (page: Page) => page.locator('.notification-bulk-actions');
const selectAll = (page: Page) => page.getByRole('checkbox', {name: 'Select all notifications on this page'});

async function pickFilter(page: Page, filter: 'repo' | 'type', item: string, param: string, value: string) {
  const dropdown = page.locator(`[data-test-id="notification-filter-${filter}"]`);
  await dropdown.click();
  await dropdown.locator('.menu .item', {hasText: item}).click();
  await page.waitForURL((u) => u.searchParams.get(param) === value); // waitForEvent('load') races WebKit's dropdown navigation
}

function act(page: Page, name: string) {
  return Promise.all([
    page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes('/notifications/bulk')),
    page.waitForEvent('load'),
    bulk(page).getByRole('button', {name}).click(),
  ]);
}

    .map((n) => [n.subject.title, n.pinned ? 'pinned' : n.unread ? 'unread' : 'read']));

  await page.goto('/notifications');
  await row(page, 'r2 pr').locator('.notification-checkbox').check();
  await row(page, 'r1 one').locator('.notification-checkbox').check();

  await page.goto('/notifications?type=read');

  await pickFilter(page, 'repo', `${owner}/r2`, 'repo', String(repoIds.r2));
  await pickFilter(page, 'type', 'Pull requests', 'source', 'pull');
  const q = new URL(page.url()).searchParams;
  expect([q.get('type'), q.get('repo'), q.get('source')]).toEqual(['read', String(repoIds.r2), 'pull']);
  await expect(rows(page)).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(rows(page)).toContainText('r2 pr');
  await capture(page, 'read-filtered');
  await page.goto(`/notifications?type=read&repo=${repoIds.r1}&source=issue`);
  await expect(rows(page)).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(rows(page)).toContainText('r1 one');
  await page.goto(`/notifications?type=read&repo=${repoIds.r2}&source=issue`); // r2 one is unread
  await expect(page.getByText('No notifications match the selected filters.')).toBeVisible();

  // Pin: a pinned row is listed on both tabs
  await page.goto('/notifications');
  await row(page, 'r2 one').locator('.notification-checkbox').check();
  await expect(bulk(page)).toContainText('1 selected');
  await act(page, 'Pin');
  await expect(page.locator('.flash-message')).toContainText('Pinned 1 notification.');
  await expect(rows(page)).toHaveCount(2);
  await page.goto('/notifications?type=read');

  const pinned = await state();
  note('after-pin', pinned);
  expect(pinned).toEqual({'r1 one': 'read', 'r1 two': 'unread', 'r2 one': 'pinned', 'r2 pr': 'read'});

  // confirmed Delete of every row on the Unread tab (the pinned one included)
  await page.goto('/notifications');
  await selectAll(page).check();
  await expect(bulk(page)).toContainText('2 selected');
  await bulk(page).getByRole('button', {name: 'Delete'}).click();

  ]);

  await capture(page, 'after-delete');
  const left = await state();
  note('after-delete', left);
  expect(left).toEqual({'r1 one': 'read', 'r2 pr': 'read'});
});

// features/issue-due-date-filter.md: every ?due= option, counts, link keeping, edges, Group by (#26),
// and the repo PR list, user dashboard /issues + /pulls and org dashboard entry points
import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '../fixtures.ts';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {capture, note} from '../evidence.ts';
import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateIssue, apiCreateMilestone, apiCreateOrg, apiCreatePR, apiCreateRepo, apiHeaders, baseUrl, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

type Seed = [title: string, offset: number | null];
type Case = [label: string, val: string, expected: string[]];

const admin = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;

// the local calendar date: the verify instance runs in the Mac's zone
function day(n: number) {
  const d = new Date(Date.now() + n * 864e5);
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}T00:00:00Z`;
}

async function apiSend(page: Page, method: string, path: string, data: unknown) {
  const response = await page.request.fetch(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1${path}`, {method, headers: apiHeaders(), data});
  expect(response.ok(), `${method} ${path}`).toBe(true);
  return response.json();
}

async function seedRepo(page: Page, owner = admin) {
  const repo = `e2e-due-${randomString(8)}`;
  if (owner === admin) await apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repo});
  else await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/orgs/${owner}/repos`, {name: repo, auto_init: true});
  return repo;
}

async function seedIssues(page: Page, owner: string, repo: string, issues: Seed[]) {
  for (const [title, offset] of issues) {
    const {index} = await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo, title});
    if (offset !== null) await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${index}/deadline`, {due_date: day(offset)});
  }
}

async function seedPRs(page: Page, owner: string, repo: string, prs: Seed[]) {
  for (const [i, [title, offset]] of prs.entries()) {
    await apiCreateFile(page.request, owner, repo, `pr-${i}.txt`, title, {newBranch: `pr-${i}`, message: title});
    const index = await apiCreatePR(page.request, owner, repo, `pr-${i}`, 'main', title);
    if (offset !== null) await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/${index}/deadline`, {due_date: day(offset)});
  }
}

const titles = async (page: Page) => (await page.locator('#issue-list .list-item-large-title').allInnerTexts()).map((t) => t.trim()).sort();

// dashboards list every repo on the instance, so keep only rows linking into one repo
const titlesIn = async (page: Page, repoWeb: string) => (await page.locator('#issue-list .list-item-large-title')
  .evaluateAll((els) => els.map((e) => [e.textContent!.trim(), e.getAttribute('href')!])))
  .filter(([, href]) => href.startsWith(`${repoWeb}/`)).map(([t]) => t).sort();

async function pick(page: Page, label: string) {
  await page.locator('.due-date-filter').click();
  await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('load'), page.locator('.due-date-filter .menu .item', {hasText: label}).first().click()]);
}

// picks each option on a list page and checks the titles, the active item and (unscoped) the open count
async function drive(page: Page, url: string, cases: Case[], scope: string | null, tag: string) {
  await page.goto(url);
  for (const [label, val, expected] of cases) {
    await pick(page, label);
    expect(new URL(page.url()).searchParams.get('due')).toBe(val);
    await expect(page.locator('.due-date-filter .active.item')).toHaveText(label);
    expect(scope ? await titlesIn(page, scope) : await titles(page)).toEqual(expected);
    if (!scope) await expect(page.locator('.small-menu-items .item').first()).toHaveText(`${expected.length} Open`, {useInnerText: true});
    await capture(page, `${tag}-due-${val}`);
  }
  await expect(page.locator('.small-menu-items .item').nth(1)).toHaveAttribute('href', new RegExp(`due=${cases.at(-1)![1]}`));
}

const issueSeed: Seed[] = [['Overdue one', -1], ['Due today one', 0], ['Due later one', 10], ['No date one', null]];
const prSeed: Seed[] = [['PR overdue', -1], ['PR due later', 10], ['PR no date', null]];

test('the repo issue list filters by every due option', async ({page}) => {
  const [repo] = await Promise.all([seedRepo(page), login(page)]);
  await seedIssues(page, admin, repo, issueSeed);
  note('stored', (await (await page.request.get(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${admin}/${repo}/issues?state=all`, {headers: apiHeaders()})).json())
    .map((i: {title: string, due_date: string}) => [i.title, i.due_date]));
  await page.goto(`/${admin}/${repo}/issues`);
  await page.locator('.due-date-filter').click();
  await expect(page.locator('.due-date-filter .menu .item')).toHaveText(['All due dates', 'Overdue', 'Due today', 'Due this week', 'Due soon', 'Has a due date', 'No due date']);
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await drive(page, `/${admin}/${repo}/issues`, [
    ['Overdue', 'overdue', ['Overdue one']],
    ['Due today', 'today', ['Due today one']],
    ['Due soon', 'soon', ['Due today one']],
    ['No due date', 'none', ['No date one']],
    ['Has a due date', 'set', ['Due later one', 'Due today one', 'Overdue one']],
  ], null, 'issues');
  await pick(page, 'Due this week'); // yesterday is last week on a Monday, so check only today's issue
  expect(await titles(page)).toContain('Due today one');
});

test('an unknown due value lists everything, and milestone pages have no due filter', async ({page}) => {
  const [repo] = await Promise.all([seedRepo(page), login(page)]);
  await seedIssues(page, admin, repo, issueSeed);
  await page.goto(`/${admin}/${repo}/issues?due=bogus`);
  expect(await titles(page)).toHaveLength(4);
  const {id} = await apiCreateMilestone(page.request, {owner: admin, repo, title: 'M'});
  await page.goto(`/${admin}/${repo}/milestone/${id}?due=overdue`);
  await expect(page.locator('.due-date-filter')).toHaveCount(0);

// features/multiselect-aria.md: label, assignee, reviewer and project pickers (combobox state, live announcements, focus),
// topics editor, branch-protection user and team pickers (aria state, announcements, delete-icon names)
import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '../fixtures.ts';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {capture} from '../evidence.ts';
import {apiCreateFile, apiCreateIssue, apiCreateOrg, apiCreatePR, apiCreateRepo, apiCreateUser, apiHeaders, baseUrl, createProject, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
const live = (page: Page) => page.locator('body > [role="status"]');

async function apiSend(page: Page, method: string, path: string, data?: unknown) {
  const response = await page.request.fetch(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1${path}`, {method, headers: apiHeaders(), data});
  expect(response.ok(), `${method} ${path}`).toBe(true);
  return response.status() === 204 ? null : response.json();
}
const apiGet = (page: Page, path: string) => apiSend(page, 'GET', path);

async function seedRepo(page: Page) {
  const repo = `e2e-multiselect-${randomString(8)}`;
  await Promise.all([apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repo}), login(page)]);
  return repo;
}

async function seedCollaborator(page: Page, repoPath: string) {
  const user = `e2e-ms-collab-${randomString(8)}`;
  await apiCreateUser(page.request, user);
  await apiSend(page, 'PUT', `/repos/${repoPath}/collaborators/${user}`, {permission: 'write'});
  return user;
}

// an issue-sidebar picker's contract: combobox, multiselectable options, announcement, focus kept, saved on close.
// aria-expanded is left out (known bug #104)
async function sidebarPick(page: Page, field: string, option: string, what: string) {
  const combo = `.issue-sidebar-combo:has(input[name="${field}"])`;
  const dropdown = page.locator(`${combo} > .ui.dropdown`);
  const item = dropdown.locator('.scrolling.menu > .item', {hasText: option});
  await expect(dropdown).toHaveAttribute('role', 'combobox');
  await dropdown.focus(); // opens the menu
  await expect(dropdown.locator('> .menu')).toHaveAttribute('aria-multiselectable', 'true');
  await expect(item).toHaveAttribute('role', 'option');
  await expect(item).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'false');
  const presses = await dropdown.evaluate((el, opt) => {
    const items = [...el.querySelectorAll('.scrolling.menu > .item:not(.filtered, .tw-hidden)')];
    return items.findIndex((i) => i.textContent!.includes(opt)) - items.findIndex((i) => i.classList.contains('selected'));
  }, option);
  for (let i = 0; i < presses; i++) await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(item).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  await expect(live(page)).toHaveText(`Selected "${option}"`);
  await expect(dropdown).toBeFocused();
  await capture(page, what);
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape'); // closing saves
  await expect(page.locator(`${combo} .ui.list`)).toContainText(option);
}

  await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo, title: 'labels'});
  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repo}/issues/1`);
  await sidebarPick(page, 'label_ids', 'bug', 'label-selected');
  await expect.poll(async () => (await apiGet(page, `/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues/1`)).labels.map((l: {name: string}) => l.name)).toEqual(['bug']);
});

});

test('branch protection user and team pickers name their options and announce changes', async ({page}) => {
  const org = `e2e-ms-org-${randomString(8)}`;

  await Promise.all([apiCreateOrg(page.request, org), login(page)]);

  for (const name of ['alpha', 'beta']) await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/orgs/${org}/teams`, {name, permission: 'write', includes_all_repositories: true, units: ['repo.code', 'repo.pulls']});
  const [first, second] = [await seedCollaborator(page, `${org}/${repo}`), await seedCollaborator(page, `${org}/${repo}`)];
  await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/repos/${org}/${repo}/branch_protections`, {rule_name: branch, enable_push: true, enable_push_whitelist: true, push_whitelist_usernames: [first], push_whitelist_teams: ['alpha']});
  await page.goto(`/${org}/${repo}/settings/branches/edit?rule_name=${branch}`);

  const pick = async (field: string, preset: string, added: string) => {
    const dropdown = page.locator(`.ui.dropdown:has(> input[name="${field}"])`);
    const search = dropdown.locator('input.search');
    const option = (t: string) => dropdown.locator('> .menu > .item', {hasText: t});
    await expect(search).toHaveAttribute('role', 'combobox');
    await expect(dropdown.locator('> .menu')).toHaveAttribute('aria-multiselectable', 'true');
    await expect(option(preset)).toHaveAttribute('role', 'option');
    await expect(option(preset)).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
    await expect(option(added)).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'false');
    await expect(dropdown.locator('.ui.label', {hasText: preset}).locator('.delete.icon')).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', `Remove item "${preset}"`); // the name, not the ID value
    await search.focus();
    await page.keyboard.type(added);
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(option(added)).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
    await expect(live(page)).toHaveText(`Selected "${added}"`); // the preset is not announced
    await expect(search).toBeFocused();
    await expect(dropdown.locator('.ui.label', {hasText: added}).locator('.delete.icon')).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', `Remove item "${added}"`);
    return option;
  };
  await pick('whitelist_users', first, second);
  const teamOption = await pick('whitelist_teams', 'alpha', 'beta');
  await capture(page, 'branch-protection-added');
  await page.keyboard.press('Backspace'); // empty search: removes the last label
  await expect(live(page)).toHaveText('Deselected "beta"');
  await expect(teamOption('beta')).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'false');
  await page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Save Rule'}).click();
  await expect.poll(async () => {
    const rule = await apiGet(page, `/repos/${org}/${repo}/branch_protections/${branch}`);
    return [rule.push_whitelist_usernames.sort(), rule.push_whitelist_teams];
  }).toEqual([[first, second].sort(), ['alpha']]);
});

```typescript
// features/org-require-2fa.md: self-required refusal, enable, banner, blocked access, API 403, compliance, enrol, last factor
import {createHmac} from 'node:crypto';
import {test, expect} from '../fixtures.ts';
import type {Browser, Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {capture, note} from '../evidence.ts';
import {apiCreateOrg, apiCreateUser, apiHeaders, apiUserHeaders, baseUrl, login, loginUser, randomString} from './utils.ts';

const POLICY = 'Require two-factor authentication for members and outside collaborators';

function totp(b32: string) { // RFC 6238: SHA1, 6 digits, 30 s
  const alphabet = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567';
  let bits = '';
  for (const c of b32.replace(/=+$/, '').toUpperCase()) bits += alphabet.indexOf(c).toString(2).padStart(5, '0');
  const key = Buffer.from(bits.match(/.{8}/g)!.map((b) => parseInt(b, 2)));
  const counter = Buffer.alloc(8);
  counter.writeBigUInt64BE(BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 30000)));
  const h = createHmac('sha1', key).update(counter).digest();
  return String((h.readUInt32BE(h[19] & 15) & 0x7fffffff) % 1e6).padStart(6, '0');
}

async function apiSend(page: Page, method: string, path: string, data?: unknown) {
  const response = await page.request.fetch(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1${path}`, {method, headers: apiHeaders(), data});
  expect(response.ok(), `${method} ${path}`).toBe(true);
  return response.status() === 204 ? null : response.json();
}

async function savePolicy(page: Page) {
  await page.getByRole('checkbox', {name: POLICY}).check();
  await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('load'), page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Update Settings'}).first().click()]);
}

// a user who is a non-admin owner of a fresh org, signed in on their own browser context
async function seedOwner(page: Page, browser: Browser) {
  const user = `e2e-tfa-${randomString(8)}`, org = `e2e-tfa-own-${randomString(8)}`;
  await Promise.all([apiCreateUser(page.request, user), apiCreateOrg(page.request, org), login(page)]);
  const owners = (await apiSend(page, 'GET', `/orgs/${org}/teams`)).find((t: {name: string}) => t.name === 'Owners');
  await apiSend(page, 'PUT', `/teams/${owners.id}/members/${user}`);
  const context = await browser.newContext({baseURL: baseUrl()});
  const userPage = await context.newPage();
  await loginUser(userPage, user);
  return {user, org, userPage};
}

async function enrol(page: Page) {
  await page.goto('/user/settings/security/two_factor/enroll');
  const secret = (await page.getByText(/Or enter the secret:/).textContent())!.split(':').pop()!.trim();
  await page.getByLabel('Passcode').fill(totp(secret));
  await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('load'), page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Verify'}).click()]);
}

test('an owner without two-factor authentication cannot require it', async ({page, browser}) => {
  const {org, userPage} = await seedOwner(page, browser);
  await userPage.goto(`/org/${org}/settings`);
  await savePolicy(userPage);
  await expect(userPage.locator('.flash-error')).toContainText('Set up two-factor authentication on your own account before requiring it');
  await capture(userPage, 'self-required-refused');
});

test('requiring two-factor authentication blocks members without it until they enrol', async ({page, browser}) => {
  const {user, userPage} = await seedOwner(page, browser);
  const collaborator = `e2e-tfa-collab-${randomString(8)}`, org = `e2e-tfa-org-${randomString(8)}`;
  await Promise.all([apiCreateUser(page.request, collaborator), apiCreateOrg(page.request, org)]);
  await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/orgs/${org}/repos`, {name: 'priv', private: true, auto_init: true});
  await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/orgs/${org}/repos`, {name: 'pub', auto_init: true});
  const team = await apiSend(page, 'POST', `/orgs/${org}/teams`, {name: 'writers', permission: 'write', includes_all_repositories: true, units: ['repo.code']});
  await apiSend(page, 'PUT', `/teams/${team.id}/members/${user}`);
  await apiSend(page, 'PUT', `/repos/${org}/priv/collaborators/${collaborator}`, {permission: 'read'});

  expect((await userPage.goto(`/${org}/priv`))!.status()).toBe(200);
  await capture(userPage, 'before');

  await page.goto(`/org/${org}/settings`);
  await expect(page.locator('#security_box')).toContainText('1 members and 1 outside collaborators');
  await savePolicy(page);
  await expect(page.locator('.flash-success')).toContainText('Organization settings have been updated.');
  await expect(page.getByRole('checkbox', {name: POLICY})).toBeChecked();
  await capture(page, 'settings-after');

  await userPage.goto('/');
  const banner = userPage.locator('.flash-error a');
  await expect(banner).toContainText('An organization you belong to requires two-factor authentication');
  await expect(banner).toHaveAttribute('href', '/user/settings/security/two_factor/enroll');
  expect((await userPage.goto(`/${org}/priv`))!.status()).toBe(404);
  expect((await userPage.goto(`/org/${org}/teams`))!.status()).toBe(404);
  expect((await userPage.goto(`/org/${org}/members`))!.status()).toBe(200); // the public view
  expect((await userPage.goto(`/${org}/pub`))!.status()).toBe(200);
  await capture(userPage, 'blocked');
  const denied = await page.request.get(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/orgs/${org}/teams`, {headers: apiUserHeaders(user)});
  expect(denied.status()).toBe(403);
  const body = await denied.text();
  expect(body).toMatch(/requires two-factor authentication/);
  note('api-403', {body});

  await page.goto(`/org/${org}/members`);
  await expect(page.locator('.ui.warning.message')).toContainText('Members without it: 1.');
  await expect(page.getByText('No access until 2FA is set up')).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(page.locator('.flash-error')).toHaveCount(0); // admins are exempt
  await capture(page, 'members');
  await page.goto(`/${org}/priv/settings/collaboration`);
  await expect(page.getByText('No access until 2FA is set up')).toHaveCount(1);

  await enrol(userPage);
  expect((await userPage.goto(`/${org}/priv`))!.status()).toBe(200);
  await userPage.goto('/');
  await expect(userPage.locator('.flash-error')).toHaveCount(0);
  await capture(userPage, 'enrolled');
});

test('an owner of an org that requires two-factor authentication cannot remove their last factor', async ({page, browser}) => {
  const {org, userPage} = await seedOwner(page, browser);
  await enrol(userPage);
  await page.goto(`/org/${org}/settings`);
  await savePolicy(page);
  await userPage.goto('/user/settings/security');
  await userPage.getByRole('button', {name: 'Disable Two-Factor Authentication'}).click();
  await userPage.locator('.ui.modal.visible').getByRole('button', {name: 'Yes'}).click(); // a copy of #disable-twofa, minus the id
  await expect(userPage.locator('.flash-error')).toContainText(`You own an organization that requires two-factor authentication (${org})`);
  await capture(userPage, 'last-factor-refused');
  await userPage.reload();
  await expect(userPage.getByRole('button', {name: 'Disable Two-Factor Authentication'})).toBeVisible(); // the factor survived
});

 `./.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md`

```text
1	---
2	name: verify
3	description: Drive the real Gitea web UI (and /api/v1) of the CSCI 435 fork to prove a change works the way a user sees it. Starts a disposable dev-mode Gitea on a free port with its own sqlite DB and admin, drives it with Playwright Test (chromium/webkit), captures screenshots + ARIA snapshots + API state, and tears down. Use after any change to templates, web_src, routers, or services, before claiming a UI/behavior change works, or when asked to screenshot or demo a feature.
4	---
5	
6	# Verify the Gitea fork
7	
8	The surface is the web UI served by `./gitea web`; the `/api/v1` REST API is the second surface and the way to seed state. The CLI (`./gitea admin ...`) is only used for setup.
9	
10	Every run gets its own instance under `.claude/verify-runs/<run-id>/` (gitignored, because all of `.claude/` is). **Never drive `http://localhost:3000`**: that is the user's own instance (`custom/conf/app.ini`, `data/`), and the user's account `mingler` must never be touched. Several runs can live side by side; each has its own port, DB, and admin.
11	
12	Two pieces, both in `.claude/skills/verify/`, and only this Mac runs them:
13	
14	- **`bin/gitea-verify`**, a stdlib-only Go binary (`*.go`, its own `go.mod`, so the repo's `go ./...` never sees it). It owns the instances: start, doctor, stop, prune, gc, and `test`, which runs Playwright on an instance. macOS-only by design (kqueue, `ps`, `lsof`). Build it with `mise run verify:bin` (every task depends on it) or `direnv exec . go build -o bin/gitea-verify .` from the skill dir.
15	- **Playwright Test** (`playwright.config.ts`, `fixtures.ts`, `specs/*.spec.ts`), using the repo's `@playwright/test`. Specs run with 4 workers on one shared instance.
16	
17	After editing either, run `mise run verify:check`: gofumpt, `go vet`, `go test`, golangci-lint (pinned to the repo flake's nixpkgs, with the local `.golangci.yml`, not Gitea's), and strict `tsc` over the fixtures and specs.
18	
19	| Command | What it does |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| `gitea-verify up [--owner <pid>] [--json]` | Writes a dev-mode `app.ini`, starts `./gitea web` on a free port, waits for `/api/v1/version`, creates admin `verify-admin` with a random [REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-password]]]. Prints `RUN_ID`, `URL`, `ARTIFACTS` and an `export GITEA_VERIFY_RUN=...` line. With `--owner`, a watchdog (kqueue `NOTE_EXIT`, its own session) tears the run down once that process exits, even on SIGKILL. |
22	| `gitea-verify doctor [run] [--json]` | Read-only health check (see Doctor). Exits non-zero on FAIL. |
23	| `gitea-verify down [run]` | Kills *our* PID only, deletes `work/` and `state.json`, moves `server.log` into the artifacts. Leaves the artifacts. An already-down run is success. |
24	| `gitea-verify prune` | Runs `down` on every run whose server already died (`up` does this first). |
25	| `gitea-verify list` | Every run, whether it is up, and where its artifacts are. |
26	| `gitea-verify gc [--keep N] [--dry-run]` | Deletes the oldest *down* run dirs, keeping the newest N (default 30). Never touches a live run or a hand-named dir such as `issue-62-before`. Run it only when the user asks for space back. |
27	| `gitea-verify test <feature\|path.spec.ts>... \| --all [flags]` | Reuses `$GITEA_VERIFY_RUN` when doctor passes; otherwise starts a fresh run (with itself as owner) and tears it down on exit. Doctors before driving, then runs `playwright test` and exits with its status. Flags after the spec names (or after `--`) go to Playwright: `--project=webkit`, `--headed`, `--debug`, `--repeat-each=3`, `--workers=1`, `-g <title>`. Defaults to `--project=chromium`. |
28	
29	`[run]` defaults to `$GITEA_VERIFY_RUN`. The binary lives at `.claude/skills/verify/bin/gitea-verify`; run it from anywhere.
30	
31	## Saved specs and mise tasks
32	
33	`specs/<feature>.spec.ts` is the executable proof for `features/<feature>.md`: it seeds its own uniquely named state, drives every entry point the feature file lists, and fails on the first mismatch. Run one before writing a new spec; extend it when your change adds behaviour, and fix it in the same change as its feature file.
34	
35	The gitignored root `mise.toml` wraps the binary (`mise tasks ls`). It declares no `[tools]` and sets `task.run_auto_install = false`, because tools come from the flake:
36	
37	| Task | Does |
38	| --- | --- |
39	| `mise run verify:build` | `direnv exec . make backend` and `make frontend` (make skips what is fresh) |
40	| `mise run verify:bin` | `go build` the binary (cached, near-instant) |
41	| `mise run verify:check` | Go format, vet, tests and lint, plus tsc (no instance needed) |
42	| `mise run verify:up` / `verify:doctor [run]` / `verify:down [run]` / `verify:list` / `verify:gc [--keep N] [--dry-run]` | the matching commands, after a build for `up` |
43	| `mise run verify:test <feature\|path>... [flags]` | build, then `gitea-verify test`; paths resolve from your cwd |
44	| `mise run verify:all [flags]` | every spec on one fresh instance, 4 workers, about 20 s; `-- --project=webkit` for WebKit |
45	
46	Every task has a `timeout`. Without mise, call `bin/gitea-verify` directly. If mise refuses the config, run `mise trust` once.
47	
48	## Launch
49	
50	1. Build what you changed. Doctor applies the Makefile's own mtime rule, so it WARNs exactly when `make` would rebuild:
51	   - Go changed: `make backend`
52	   - `templates/` or `options/` changed: nothing to build. The binary has no `bindata` tag, so it reads them from disk, and dev mode reloads templates
53	   - `web_src/` changed: `make frontend` (writes `public/assets`, served via `STATIC_ROOT_PATH`)
54	   - `pnpm` and the pinned `go` come from the repo's flake dev shell. The agent's Bash shell doesn't load direnv, so run `direnv exec . make frontend` (same for `make backend`)
55	2. For a one-shot proof, skip `up`: `gitea-verify test <feature>` starts and stops its own instance (about 1-2 s). To poke at an instance across several commands, run `gitea-verify up` and then prefix later commands with `GITEA_VERIFY_RUN=<id>`, because shell state does not persist between Bash calls.
56	3. Playwright launches browsers, so run `test` with the Bash sandbox disabled.
57	
58	The instance runs `RUN_MODE = dev`, so `/devtest/*` component pages exist (`/devtest` lists them). Captcha is off and the install is locked. `EVENT_SOURCE_UPDATE_TIME` stays at its 10 s default: `tools/test-e2e.sh`'s 500 ms makes the notifications page re-render its filter dropdowns mid-click.
59	
60	## Doctor
61	
62	`gitea-verify doctor <id>` checks:
63	
64	- the PID is this run's `gitea web` (matched by its unique `--config` path, so a reused PID never counts)
65	- `up` finished (`ready` in `state.json`)
66	- that PID owns the port (not some other server)
67	- `/api/v1/version` answers
68	- `/devtest` is served (dev mode)
69	- `verify-admin` authenticates
70	- `./gitea` freshness: WARN when any Go source in the Makefile's `GO_DIRS` (or a root `*.go`) is newer than `./gitea`
71	- frontend freshness: WARN when anything in `web_src/js`, `web_src/css`, `vite.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` is newer than `public/assets/.vite/manifest.json`
72	
73	A WARN means the instance runs old code. Rebuild and restart before proving anything about your change. A proof made against a stale binary proves nothing. `test` still drives on a WARN, but repeats it under `stale build` in its summary. Doctor is an mtime check: a bundle built on another branch can be newer than this branch's sources and still pass. After switching branches, run `make frontend` before trusting a result.
74	
75	Instances listen on `127.0.0.1` only. `state.json` is data (mode 600, written atomically), and the fixtures refuse a run until `ready` is set. A corrupt `state.json` shows as `corrupt` in `list`, and `prune` tears that run down instead of failing.
76	
77	## Drive
78	
79	A saved spec, or a one-off one in the scratchpad, imports the fixtures:

87	  await api('POST', `/repos/${user}/verify-issues/issues`, {title: 'Verify comment flow'});
88	  await page.goto(`/${user}/verify-issues/issues/1`, {waitUntil: 'load'});
89	  await s.capture('before');                       // NN-before.png + NN-before.aria.yml, attached to the report
90	  // ...the user action, through the UI...
91	  await s.capture('after');
92	  s.note('api-state', await api('GET', `/repos/${user}/verify-issues/issues/1`)); // side effect, second view
93	  const anon = await session({name: 'anonymous', login: false}); // or {name, user, [REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-password]]]}; viewport, deviceScaleFactor: 2
94	  await anon.page.goto('/', {waitUntil: 'load'});

97	
98	Run it with `gitea-verify test <scratchpad>/specs/comment.spec.ts`. Scratchpad specs must share one directory (it becomes Playwright's `testDir`). `test` writes a `{"type": "module"}` `package.json` there if one is missing, because Playwright loads a spec as ESM only under one, and `fixtures.ts` is ESM.
99	
100	The fixtures are:
101	
102	- `page`: verify-admin, signed in once per run through the real login form (`global-setup.ts`, saved under `work/`).
103	- `s`: evidence for `page`, under `artifacts/<spec name>/`.
104	- `api(method, path, body?)`: the admin's REST client, with a 30 s timeout. Add `?sudo=<user>` to act as someone else; the browser cookie doesn't authenticate `/api/v1`.
105	- `session(opts)`: another context with its own evidence directory. Each has `{page, user, capture, note, dir}`.
106	- `user`, `run`: the admin login and the run's state.
107	- An automatic fixture fails the test on any uncaught page error, in every context it opened, and writes `js-errors.json`.
108	
109	`expect` gives Playwright's auto-waiting assertions: prefer `await expect(locator).toHaveText(...)` to reading a value once and comparing it. A spec's timeout is 180 s, actions time out at 10 s, navigations at 20 s, and `retries` is 0, because a proof that passes on retry is not a proof. On failure Playwright keeps a trace: `pnpm exec playwright show-trace <artifacts>/playwright/<test>/trace.zip`, or `show-report <artifacts>/report`.
110	
111	Rules that each cost a failed run before:
112	
113	- **`waitUntil: 'load'`, never `'networkidle'`.** Signed-in pages hold an SSE connection open, so `networkidle` never fires.
114	- **Navigating from a Fomantic dropdown item:** wait with `page.waitForURL(...)` for the URL the item produces, not `Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('load'), click])`. In WebKit the navigation can start before the `load` listener is attached.
115	- **Browsers:** chromium and webkit work. Firefox 1532 hangs at launch on this Mac (a sandbox_extension error). It has no project; CI checks it.
116	- **WebKit skips buttons on Tab** (like Safari). Keyboard-Tab proofs run in chromium. WebKit also reports a fetch cut off by navigation as `TypeError: Load failed`; the fixtures ignore exactly that message, on WebKit only.
117	- **Locators:** use the same handles the e2e suite uses: `getByRole(..., {name})`, `getByLabel`, `getByPlaceholder`. `tests/e2e/*.test.ts` has a working selector for most pages, so read the matching test before inventing one.
118	- **Fomantic dropdowns** (`.ui.dropdown`) are not ARIA menus. Click the `.ui.dropdown` and then `.menu .item` with `hasText`. Scope to the enclosing form or group, because pages often have several dropdowns.
119	- **Shared instance:** specs run in parallel on one instance and may rerun on it. Use unique names, and scope instance-wide lists (dashboards, the admin's notifications) to your own repo, for example by row link, not by title.
120	- **Seed with `api()`, act with `page`.** The proof must go through the UI path the user takes; the API is for setup and for reading back the stored result.
121	
122	The feature map is [`features/README.md`](features/README.md), with a saved spec per feature in `specs/`. Read the matching feature file, and run its spec, before you drive.
123	
124	## Evidence
125	
126	Artifacts go to `.claude/verify-runs/<id>/artifacts/`:
127	
128	- `<name>/NN-<what>.png`: full-page screenshot. The footer shows the build version, `1.27.3+csci435-...-g<sha>`, which identifies the build. A non-chromium run writes `<name>-webkit/`.
129	- `<name>/NN-<what>.aria.yml`: an ARIA snapshot of the same moment. Assert names and states against this, not against pixels.
130	- `<name>/NN-<what>.json`: from `note()`, the stored state read back through the API.
131	- `<spec>/js-errors.json`: uncaught page errors. Anything other than `[]` fails the test.
132	- `report/`: Playwright's HTML report, with the captures attached. `playwright/`: traces and error context for failures.
133	- `server.log`: moved here by `down`.
134	
135	Proof standards:
136	
137	- Exercise the real user path: clicks, keys, form submits. Do not call internal JS, use test-only endpoints, or set state directly.
138	- Capture both the action and the resulting state, not only the final screen: before, after, and the API read-back of the side effect (row stored, issue state changed, comment exists).
139	- When a feature has several entry points, the map lists them. Driving one entry point does not verify the others, so report which one you drove.
140	- Prove a new spec fails: break the behaviour's key line, rebuild, and watch it go red. Edit source with Python or the Edit tool, not `sed -i ''`: `sed` here is GNU, which reads `''` as the script and rewrites the file unchanged, bumping its mtime.
141	- For PR screenshots, Read the PNG to check it shows what you claim, then follow the screenshot conventions in memory (`commit-and-pr-conventions`).
142	
143	## Cleanup
144	
145	A fresh run from `test` is always torn down, including on Ctrl-C and on SIGKILL (the watchdog does it). After `up`, run `gitea-verify down <id>`. It kills only the PID recorded at launch: never `pkill gitea`, which would also kill the user's :3000 instance. `gitea-verify list` shows stragglers. Delete artifact dirs (`gc`) only when the user asks.
146	
147	## Isolation notes
148	
149	- Each run's data lives under `work/`, and it never reads `custom/conf/app.ini` or `data/`.
150	- `verify-admin`'s [REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-password]]] is random per run and stored in `state.json` (mode 600). It is throwaway, but still don't print it. The fixtures read it for you.
151	- The user's `claude-dev` account and `$GITEA_DEV_*` belong to the :3000 instance. This skill never needs them.
152

```text
# Gitea fork verification map

This directory is the maintained source for verifying user-facing Gitea behaviour. Read this index, then the matching feature file, then run its spec. The driver, launch, and cleanup steps are in [`../SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md).

## Baseline preconditions

- A run from `gitea-verify test` (fresh, torn down after) or `gitea-verify up` with `GITEA_VERIFY_RUN` set (reused). Never drive `localhost:3000`.
- `gitea-verify doctor` passes, with no freshness WARN for the code you changed.
- The instance starts empty: one admin, `verify-admin`, and no repos. Each spec seeds its own state through `api()`.

## Driving conventions

- Saved specs live in `../specs/`; one-off specs are `.spec.ts` files in the scratchpad. Both import `test` and `expect` from `fixtures.ts`.
- Prefer roles and accessible names (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`, `getByPlaceholder`). Fall back to the CSS hooks the e2e suite already uses, such as `.comment-body` and `#issue-actions`.
- Navigate with `waitUntil: 'load'`.
- Give each spec its own repo and user names (suffix a timestamp or random hex). Specs run in parallel on one instance and rerun on it, so scope anything instance-wide (dashboards, the admin's notifications) to the spec's own repo.

## Proof and skip reporting

- Capture before and after (`s.capture`) and read the stored result back (`s.note` plus `api('GET', ...)`).
- `js-errors.json` must be `[]`; the fixtures fail the test otherwise.
- Name the feature ID and the entry point you drove. A skipped entry point is reported as skipped, not as covered by another one.
- A path you could not reach is reported with the command you tried and the precondition that was missing.

## Specs

Each feature file has an executable twin at `../specs/<same-name>.spec.ts`; `bin/gitea-verify test <name>` (or `mise run verify:test <name>`) runs it. When a feature file changes, change its spec too, and rerun it.

## Feature entry contract

Each feature file has an H1 and a one-paragraph description, followed by four H2s in order: `Sub-features`, `How to get to it (user POV)`, `Driving it`, and `Gotchas`.

## Features

- [Sign in](./sign-in.md): the login form, a bad [REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-password]]], sign-out.
- [Issue comment and close](./issue-comment-close.md): comment, close with one of four reasons, reopen, and bulk close from the list.
- [aria-menu](./aria-menu.md): the course's Fomantic-free menu button (#61), on the demo, navbar, footer and comment menus (#62), plus names on icon-only Fomantic triggers (#64).
- [Pull request create](./pull-request-create.md): compare page to an open PR.
- [Milestone burndown](./milestone-burndown.md): the burndown chart, summary, changes list and pull request toggle (#14).
- [Issue due-date filter](./issue-due-date-filter.md): the `Due date` list filter (#34), plus label-scope grouping (#26).
---
name: verify-map
description: Keep the CSCI 435 Gitea fork's `/verify` feature map honest. Two modes. `add` writes a new feature file, its asserting spec and its index line when an issue or PR ships user-facing behaviour, then proves it live. `audit` checks every mapped feature against source and drives all of them live, fixing doc and harness drift and reporting product regressions. Use for "add #57 to the verify map", "write a verify spec for this feature", "map this feature", "audit the verify skill", "is the feature map still right", /maintain-verification-skill, /create-verification-skill, or after merging a sprint PR that changed a page the map covers.
---

# Maintain the verify feature map

`/verify` (`.claude/skills/verify/`) drives a disposable Gitea. Its feature map is `features/<name>.md`, and each file has an executable twin, `specs/<name>.spec.ts`. This skill adds entries to that map and audits it. Read `../verify/SKILL.md` before you drive anything. It owns launch, doctor, the fixtures API and cleanup, and this skill does not repeat them.

The whole `.claude/` tree is gitignored, and so is `mise.toml`. Map edits therefore never become a commit or a PR. You finish by reporting to the user.

## Files one feature owns

Keep all three consistent, because `scripts/check-map.sh` fails on any mismatch:

1. `features/<name>.md`: an H1 and one paragraph that names the issue and PR numbers, then four H2s in this order: `Sub-features`, `How to get to it (user POV)`, `Driving it`, `Gotchas`. Copy the shape of `features/notifications.md`.
2. `specs/<name>.spec.ts`: starts with a `// features/<name>.md: <what it covers>` comment. It imports `test` and `expect` from `../fixtures.ts`, seeds uniquely named state through `api()`, drives every entry point the feature file lists through `page` (or `session()` for another account), and fails on the first mismatch. Prefer `expect(...)` with auto-wait to reading a value once and comparing it. Specs share one instance with three others running in parallel, so scope anything instance-wide to the spec's own repo.
3. A line under `## Features` in `features/README.md`: `- [Title](./<name>.md): what it covers (#issue)`.
Run `.claude/skills/verify-map/scripts/check-map.sh` from the repo root after any edit. It exits 0 when the three sets agree and every feature file has the H2 contract. No mise task per feature: `mise run verify:test <name>` runs any one.

## Edit scope

Edit only `.claude/skills/verify/` (its SKILL.md, features, specs, fixtures and Go sources) and the `verify:*` blocks in `mise.toml`. Never edit product code here. When the app no longer does what the map says, decide which case it is:

- **Doc drift**: the map is wrong about working behaviour. Fix the map.
- **Harness gap**: the behaviour works but the spec or `fixtures.ts` can't reach it. Fix the harness. After a Go or fixtures change, run `mise run verify:check`, and document new usage in `verify/SKILL.md`.
- **Product regression**: the app is broken. Never weaken a spec to make it pass. Report the regression to the user with the failing assertion and the artifact path. If they want an issue filed, draft it in the bug-report format from `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## Mode `add`: map a new feature

Use this mode when an issue or PR adds or changes something a user can see. Usually that's the user's own sprint work (#57, #60, #95, #65 and so on) right after implementing it.

1. **Ground it in the change.** Run `gh issue view <n>` and `gh pr view <n> --json title,body,files`. Read the diff for the routes, templates and `web_src` it touches. Then read the matching `tests/e2e/*.test.ts`, because its selectors already work. If an existing feature file covers the same page (for example a new `g` key belongs in `shortcuts`), extend that file and its spec rather than adding a new one.
2. **Write the feature file** from the user's point of view: the sub-features, every entry point (navbar, keyboard, URL, settings page), the selectors that pin them down, the preconditions to seed, and the gotchas you hit. Reference issue and PR numbers.
3. **Write the spec.** Cover every sub-feature and entry point the file lists. Capture `before` and `after`, and read the side effect back through `api()` with `s.note()`.
4. **Wire it up.** Add the README index line, then run `scripts/check-map.sh`.
5. **Prove it live.** Build what the change touched, as `verify/SKILL.md` Launch describes. Run `mise run verify:test <name>`, or `bin/gitea-verify test <name>` without mise, then `--repeat-each=2` on one instance to prove it reruns cleanly. A spec you never ran is a draft. Read at least one captured PNG to confirm it shows what the spec claims.
6. **Prove it fails.** Comment out the behaviour's key line (with the Edit tool or Python, not `sed -i ''`), or check out the commit before the feature, and confirm the spec goes red. Restore the code and rebuild before you stop. A spec that passes against old code proves nothing. If this step isn't practical (a migration-heavy change, say), skip it and tell the user you did.

## Mode `audit`: check the whole map
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Check that the verify feature map's three views agree: features/*.md, specs/*.spec.ts and
# the README index. Also checks each feature file's H2 contract.
# Run from the repo root. Exits 1 and prints every mismatch; exits 0 silently except a summary.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
V="$ROOT/.claude/skills/verify"
[ -d "$V" ] || { echo "missing $V: /verify is local-only, restore it first" >&2; exit 1; }

names() { sed -E 's/(\.spec)?\.[a-z]+$//' | sort -u; }
features=$(cd "$V/features" && ls *.md | grep -vx README.md | names)
specs=$(cd "$V/specs" && ls *.spec.ts | names)
indexed=$(grep -oE '\]\(\./[^)]+\.md\)' "$V/features/README.md" | sed -E 's/.*\.\/(.*)\.md\)/\1/' | sort -u)

fail=0
diffset() { # label, expected list, actual list
  local missing extra
  missing=$(comm -23 <(echo "$2") <(echo "$3")); extra=$(comm -13 <(echo "$2") <(echo "$3"))
  [ -n "$missing" ] && { echo "$1 missing: $(echo $missing)"; fail=1; }
  [ -n "$extra" ] && { echo "$1 extra (no feature file): $(echo $extra)"; fail=1; }
}
diffset "specs/" "$features" "$specs"
diffset "README index" "$features" "$indexed"

want=$'Sub-features\nHow to get to it (user POV)\nDriving it\nGotchas'
for f in $features; do
  got=$(sed -n 's/^## //p' "$V/features/$f.md")
  [ "$got" = "$want" ] || { echo "features/$f.md: H2s are [$(echo "$got" | paste -sd '|' -)], want [$(echo "$want" | paste -sd '|' -)]"; fail=1; }
  [ "$(head -1 "$V/features/$f.md" | cut -c1-2)" = "# " ] || { echo "features/$f.md: first line is not an H1"; fail=1; }
  [ -f "$V/specs/$f.spec.ts" ] && ! head -1 "$V/specs/$f.spec.ts" | grep -q "features/$f.md" && { echo "specs/$f.spec.ts: first line should name features/$f.md"; fail=1; }
done

[ $fail = 0 ] && echo "map ok: $(echo $features | wc -w | tr -d ' ') features"
exit $fail
```

```text
Label picker keeps aria-expanded="true" after Escape closes it
OPEN
## Observed Behavior
Escape closes the label picker's list in the issue sidebar, but the picker keeps `aria-expanded="true"`. A screen reader announces the picker as expanded while its list is closed.

The picker is a Fomantic dropdown with `role="combobox"`. Gitea's ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts` sets its `aria-expanded`.

## Expected Behavior
`aria-expanded` changes to `false` when Escape closes the list, as it does when the picker loses focus.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Sign in, and open an issue in a repository that has at least one label.
2. Press Tab until the **Labels** picker in the sidebar has focus. The list opens.
3. Wait at least 150 ms.
4. Press Escape.
5. Inspect the picker. The list is hidden, focus is still on the picker, and `aria-expanded` is `"true"`.

If you press Escape less than 100 ms after the picker gets focus, `aria-expanded` changes to `"false"`. Step 3 avoids that case.

## Additional Information
- Found on commit `4f8e6ec205` in Chromium and WebKit, through Playwright on macOS.
- Cause, from reading the code: `refreshAriaActiveItem` in `dropdown.ts` sets `aria-expanded`. Only the `focus`, `blur` and `mouseup` listeners and the arrow-key `keyup` listener call it. No listener calls it when Escape closes the list.
- Focusing the picker also fires a `blur` listener, which schedules `refreshAriaActiveItem` 100 ms later. An Escape inside those 100 ms is corrected by that refresh. This hides the bug from a test that presses Escape immediately.
- The test `issue label picker reports collapsed after Escape` in `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts` records this bug. It is marked `test.fail()` and links to this issue. When the bug is fixed, the test passes, and Playwright reports it as a failure. Remove the `test.fail()` line in the same PR as the fix.
- Found by #65.

## Design Decision
### Decision 1: refresh the ARIA state when the dropdown module hides
**Decision:** In `delegateDropdownModule` in `dropdown.ts`, wrap the Fomantic dropdown module's own `hide` method. The wrapper calls the original `hide` with the same arguments, then calls `deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100)`. The 100 ms delay matches the `blur` listener, which waits for the hide animation. Confirmed by the implementer, @Jack-Donohue.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Wrap Fomantic's `onHide` setting, the way the function wraps `onLabelCreate`. This was the first proposal. A later `dropdown('setting', {onHide})` call replaces the wrapper, because Fomantic merges new settings over old ones (`dropdown.js:3732-3736`). The label picker makes that call (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:231-236`), and so do the `.jump` dropdowns (`common-page.ts:73-81`). The fix would miss the exact picker this issue is about.
- (b) Add Escape to the `keyup` listener that refreshes the state on arrow keys.
- (c) Watch the menu's `class` attribute with a `MutationObserver`, and refresh the state on every change.

**Rationale:** Escape and every other internal close call `module.hide()` (`dropdown.js:1649-1651`). Calls such as `$dropdown.dropdown('hide')` also go through the same module object, so one wrapper catches every hide. It isn't a setting, so later `setting` calls can't replace it, and `dropdown.ts:133-147` already patches the module the same way for `set.direction`. Option (b) is smaller but fixes only Escape. Option (c) catches every hide, but it runs on every animation class change and adds an observer to every dropdown on the page.

**Consequences:** `module.hide()` still calls `settings.onHide` itself, so the label picker's save (`repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts:209-211`) runs unchanged. The existing e2e test `issue labels can be selected and deselected by keyboard` checks this, since it presses Escape and checks the saved list. The patch depends on a Fomantic internal method name, the same risk the `set.direction` patch already carries. A Fomantic upgrade must recheck both. The fix PR adds a Vitest case in `dropdown.test.ts` and removes the `test.fail()` line from `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts`.


## Scope
small

243 web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {html, htmlRaw} from '../utils/html.ts';
import {localUserSettings} from './user-settings.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence
const enabledSettingKey = 'keyboard-shortcuts-enabled';

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  alwaysOn?: boolean, // still runs when the user has turned shortcuts off
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section' | 'alwaysOn'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;
  // kept in memory as well, so the switch works for this page even where storage throws
  private enabled = localUserSettings.getBoolean(enabledSettingKey, true);

  isEnabled(): boolean {
    return this.enabled;
  }

  setEnabled(enabled: boolean) {
    this.enabled = enabled;
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    localUserSettings.setBoolean(enabledSettingKey, enabled);
  }

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section, alwaysOn}) => ({keys, description, section, alwaysOn}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field, or belongs to an open dialog, not the page behind it
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable || document.querySelector('dialog[open]')) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    // WCAG 2.1.4: a dictated word must not run shortcuts, so with them off only the always-on ones match
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter((s) => isActive(s) && (this.enabled || s.alwaysOn));
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function areShortcutsEnabled(): boolean {
  return globalRegistry.isEnabled();
}

export function setShortcutsEnabled(enabled: boolean) {
  globalRegistry.setEnabled(enabled);
}

// Groups shortcuts by section in the order each section first appears, the default section first.
// A shortcut without a section belongs to the default one.
export function groupShortcuts(shortcuts: ShortcutInfo[], defaultSection: string): Map<string, ShortcutInfo[]> {
  const groups = new Map<string, ShortcutInfo[]>([[defaultSection, []]]);
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    const section = shortcut.section ?? defaultSection;
    if (!groups.has(section)) groups.set(section, []);
    groups.get(section)!.push(shortcut);
  }
  return groups;
}

function renderShortcutKeys(keys: string): string {
  return keys.split(' ').map((key) => html`<kbd>${key.toUpperCase()}</kbd>`).join('');
}

export function initShortcutLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement) {

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutLink', initShortcutLink);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutHelp', initShortcutHelp);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // initShortcutKbd registers it, so pressing the matching key focuses the sibling input.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Ctrl/Alt/Cmd+Escape is left alone
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-27 02:31:34Z)**_

No existing issue or open PR triggers it in a way a mouse or normal keyboard user would notice. One kind of user, though, could hit it through code that's already merged.

**What the measurement showed**, in Chromium with both the Close button and Escape:
- When the dialog closes, the browser puts focus back on the button that opened it straight away.
- The `close` event fires 7–18 ms later, and only then does `opener.focus()` run. Because the browser has already restored focus, that call does nothing useful in Chromium.
- So focus is stolen only when something else takes focus inside that window of about 20 ms. After a 1 s pause, clicking into the search box and pressing Escape left focus on the page itself, as it should.

This contradicts my memory note that Escape in the search box sent focus back to the button "every time after closing with the dialog's Close button". It didn't reproduce, so I'll correct the note.

**Which work could trigger it.** Anything that moves focus within about 20 ms of the dialog closing. Shortcuts can't run while the dialog is open, so only a keypress right after closing counts:

| Issue / PR | Can it trigger it? |
| --- | --- |
| #56 `s`/`t`, #58 `g`, #59 `c`, #95 `r` (merged) | **Yes, through fast input only.** For example, Escape then `s` within ~20 ms: `s` focuses the search box, then the late `close` event pulls focus back to the button and the next keys are lost. People type that fast only rarely, but voice-control and macro tools (Dragon, Talon, Voice Control) send key sequences in one burst. |
| #60 / PR #121 | Doesn't trigger it: its checkbox sits inside the dialog and doesn't close it. But voice users are exactly who #60 is for (WCAG 2.1.4), so it's the issue most affected by the bug. |
| #108–#110 aria-menu migrations (open) | Only like the shortcuts: a menu opened by a fast key right after closing. Nothing new. |
| #104 | No: different code (Fomantic dropdown), no dialog. |
| PR #122 (#52), PR #123 (#98), #118 | No: their diffs add no dialogs, `.focus()` calls or shortcuts. |

The simplest fix is to drop `opener.focus()`, or to run it only when focus is still on the page itself or inside the dialog. Either way the race goes away. One gap: I measured Chromium only. The code comment says browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes, so WebKit and Firefox would need checking before removing the line outright.
